newsitem.title: USA: National Steel says workers win wage hikes.
newsitem.headline: National Steel says workers win wage hikes.

text.p: National Steel Corp said on Thursday an arbitrator awarded wage increases for 7,000 company employees represented by the United Steelworkers.

Under the award, union workers will get a wage hike of $0.50 per hour retroactive to August 1, 1996. Increases of $0.25 per hour will be made on August 1, 1997 and on August 1, 1998, the company said.
In addition, $500 lump-sum bonuses will be paid on May 1 in 1998 and 1999, the steelmaker said.
The addition of one holiday that began in 1993 will be continued throughout the agreement's term, it said.
"No other details will be disclosed pending agreement on contract language," the company said in a release dated October 31.
The company could not be reached for further comment on Friday morning. National Steel shares were off 1/8 to 8-1/2.
